content:
Rain hits the concrete. Hard. Cold.

The fog rolls in. Thick. Gray. It swallows the pier. Swallows the lights.

One lamp flickers. Dies. Darkness takes the rest.

My coffee is black. Bitter. Gone cold. I sip. It burns.

A creak from the crane. Metal on metal. Old bones shifting.

Wind howls. Low. Mean. It tears at my coat. Cuts through the wool.

I check the watch. 3:14 AM. Time is dead here.

No boats. No voices. Just the water. Slapping the pilings. Rhythm. Endless. Wet.

I light a cigarette. The flame jumps. Dies in the gust. I try again. It holds.

Smoke rises. Thin. Pale. It vanishes into the mist.

My eyes sting. Salt air. Exhaustion.

I lean against the railing. Iron is ice-cold. Burns my palm.

Watch the water. Watch the dark. Wait for dawn. Or wait for trouble.

Either way, I stay.
